ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small block placed at the edge of a circular horizontal turntable accelerates with the turntable. When the rotational speed reaches a certain value, the block slides off the turntable and begins to perform projectile motion. It is known that the radius of the turntable is $R{=}0.5\mathrm{m}$, the height from the horizontal ground is $H{=}0.8\mathrm{m}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the turntable is $\mu{=}0.2$, and the maximum static friction force on the object is equal to the kinetic friction force. The gravitational acceleration is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the angular velocity of the small block when it slides off the table?
2. What is the horizontal range when the small block hits the ground?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal circular turntable, with the center marked as O, and a small block located at the edge of the turntable; from O to the small block there is a dashed radius marked as R. From below the edge of the turntable to the ground there is a vertical dashed height H. After the small block leaves the edge, it undergoes projectile motion along an arc, and the horizontal distance between the landing point and the point directly below the edge is marked as s. The figure also shows an arrow indicating that the turntable rotates about a vertical axis. Reasoning: Before the small block slips, it moves in circular motion together with the turntable. In the inertial frame, the required centripetal force is provided by static friction, that is, f_s = mω²R. When it is just about to slide off, the static friction reaches its maximum value; the problem states that the maximum static friction is equal to the kinetic friction, so f_max = μmg. Therefore mω²R = μmg, and eliminating m gives ω = sqrt(μg/R). Substituting μ = 0.2, g = 10 m/s², R = 0.5 m, gives ω = sqrt(0.2×10/0.5) = sqrt(4) = 2 rad/s. When the small block leaves the turntable, its velocity is in the horizontal direction, with magnitude v = ωR = 2×0.5 = 1 m/s. Then it undergoes projectile motion from height H = 0.8 m, and the vertical direction satisfies H = (1/2)gt², so t = sqrt(2H/g) = sqrt(2×0.8/10) = sqrt(0.16) = 0.4 s. The horizontal displacement s = vt = 1×0.4 = 0.4 m.

method.method_draft: Use an inertial-frame force-balance route. First read the diagram as a horizontal turntable with the block at the rim, center marked O, radius R from O to the block, a vertical drop H from the table edge to the ground, and a horizontal flight distance s after the block leaves. From the text take R=0.5 m, H=0.8 m, μ=0.2, g=10 m/s², and the fact that maximum static friction equals kinetic friction. While the block co-rotates without slipping, static friction supplies the required centripetal force: f_s=mω²R. At the instant of sliding, f_s reaches f_max=μmg, so mω²R=μmg and ω=sqrt(μg/R)=2 rad/s. Then use the diagram’s projectile stage: the block leaves horizontally from height H with speed v=ωR=1 m/s. The fall time is t=sqrt(2H/g)=0.4 s, so the horizontal range is s=vt=0.4 m.

A small block placed at the edge of a circular horizontal turntable accelerates with the turntable. When the rotational speed reaches a certain value, the block slides off the turntable and begins to perform projectile motion. It is known that the radius of the turntable is $R{=}0.5\mathrm{m}$, the height from the horizontal ground is $H{=}0.8\mathrm{m}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the turntable is $\mu{=}0.2$, and the maximum static friction force on the object is equal to the kinetic friction force. The gravitational acceleration is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the angular velocity of the small block when it slides off the table?
2. What is the horizontal range when the small block hits the ground?

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal circular turntable, the center is labeled O, and a small block is located at the edge of the turntable; from O to the small block there is a dashed radius labeled R. From below the edge of the turntable to the ground there is a vertical dashed height H; after the small block leaves the edge, it undergoes projectile motion along an arc, and the horizontal distance between the landing point and the point directly below the edge is labeled s. The figure also draws an arrow showing the turntable rotating around the vertical axis.

Reasoning: Before the small block slips, it moves in circular motion together with the turntable. In the inertial frame, the required centripetal force is provided by static friction, that is f_s = mω²R. Just as it is about to slide away, the static friction reaches its maximum value; the problem states that the maximum static friction force is equal to the kinetic friction force, so f_max = μmg. Therefore mω²R = μmg, canceling m gives ω = sqrt(μg/R). Substituting μ = 0.2, g = 10 m/s², R = 0.5 m, gives ω = sqrt(0.2×10/0.5) = sqrt(4) = 2 rad/s.

When the small block leaves the turntable, its velocity is in the horizontal direction, with magnitude v = ωR = 2×0.5 = 1 m/s. It then undergoes projectile motion from height H = 0.8 m; in the vertical direction it satisfies H = (1/2)gt², so t = sqrt(2H/g) = sqrt(2×0.8/10) = sqrt(0.16) = 0.4 s. The horizontal displacement s = vt = 1×0.4 = 0.4 m.
